title: GAN vs Diffusion vs Flow Matching
interviewAnswer: GANs use adversarial training and usually sample in one/few passes; diffusion learns a reverse corruption process; flow matching learns a transport velocity field. Compare them by stability, sample quality/diversity, inference speed and controllability—not by a single winner.
why: Modern GenAI interviews often ask you to compare model families based on objective, sampling, diversity, stability and controllability rather than declaring one universally best.
intuition: GANs learn through a discriminator game, diffusion learns to reverse corruption, and flow matching learns a continuous velocity field transporting noise to data.
deepDive: GANs often provide fast one-pass generation but can be unstable and mode-collapse. Diffusion uses a known corruption path and iterative denoising; training is generally stable but sampling may require many network evaluations. Flow matching trains a vector field along chosen probability paths and generates by integrating an ODE; path/solver choices influence efficiency. Architecture and training paradigm are separate: a DiT-like transformer can be used with diffusion or flow-matching objectives.
workedExample: For interactive low-latency image generation, a GAN can be attractive if quality/diversity are sufficient. For high-fidelity controllable generation, diffusion/flow models may be easier to train and condition but cost more inference compute.
commonMistakes: Saying MMDiT and flow matching are the same concept.
Assuming diffusion never has mode-coverage issues or GANs are obsolete.
Comparing generation speed without fixing hardware, steps and resolution.
followUps: Can a transformer be used in both diffusion and flow matching?
When would you choose a GAN today?
production: Choose the family from latency, controllability, data, hardware and quality constraints. Profile end-to-end serving cost rather than comparing model families abstractly.
